variants.note: Broad oak crown in several heavy lobes, rough visible trunk and flared roots; warm upper planes sit over deep leaf pockets.
Smoother beech crown with narrower linked masses and a clean pale trunk entering leaf litter.
Slender pale birch trunk and a lighter narrow crown, with small dark bark breaks; use the birch size class on promotion.
Heavy pollard head with long drooping willow shoots above a wet-bank root flare; use the willow size class rather than the broadleaf envelope.
Low branching orchard tree with a broad accessible canopy and a legible trunk fork; fruit, if shown, remains quiet stage dressing.

todo: Scope: shared. Reusable across the listed places; preserve site-specific assembly and state.
Purpose: Complete mixed tree edges from the existing oak, beech and birch rather than add another forest painter.

Visual brief: Each crown is an organic scalloped volume with warm upper-left planes, cool depth between leaf masses, a trunk visibly entering its own roots and a crown-shaped cast shadow. Pollard and orchard forms differ in silhouette.
Geometry: proposed visual envelope only; Claude supplies exact foot, solid footprint, overhang, interaction anchors and any deck after review.
Implementation: concept only, outside the live piece library. Do not place, bake or grant gameplay until reviewed and approved.
Reuse: woodland_oak, woodland_beech, woodland_birch, woodland_willow, woodland_sapling; do not create near-duplicate entries after their approvals.
Size: broadleaf 148-311 art px high and 133-259 wide; birch/willow variants must use their own size classes, not the nominal broadleaf envelope.
Draw three or more species/sizes for a tree wall; never more than three identical crowns consecutively.
Lighting: upper-left key light; shade each material and facing for that light. The lit-picture reference is deferred until art exists.
